```{r}
#| label: setup
#| message: false
library(tidyverse)   # readr, dplyr, ggplot2 ...
library(pROC)
theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 12))

batches <- read_csv("data-raw/crystallization/crystallization_batches.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
new_batches <- read_csv("data-raw/crystallization/new_batches.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
cost_rescue <- 1500    # EUR, switching a batch to the slow cooling program
cost_rework <- 12000   # EUR, redissolving and recrystallizing a failed batch
```

## 2. Cleaning

<!-- Record every decision here, and in the cleaning log at the end. -->

```{r}
#| label: clean
clean <- function(d) {
  d |>
    mutate(
      # seed_temp_C = ...,                         # reason: ...
      impurity_missing = as.integer(is.na(impurity_ppm)),
      fail = as.integer(particle_test == "fail")   # (new_batches has no particle_test yet)
    )
}
# train <- clean(batches) |> select(-filtration_time_h)   # reason: ...
```

## 3. Comparing methods

<!-- 10-fold CV on the 1,000 batches, stratified by the outcome, with imputation and scaling
     inside the folds. At least: main-effects logistic, lasso, kNN, SVM, neural network, and
     a model built from process insight (an interaction, a curved term, or a GAM).
     Report the CV AUC and log loss of each. -->

```{r}
#| label: folds
#| eval: false
set.seed(2026)
fold <- integer(nrow(train))
for (cl in 0:1) {                                  # stratified: assign folds within each class
  idx <- which(train$fail == cl)
  fold[idx] <- sample(rep(1:10, length.out = length(idx)))
}
cv_predict <- function(fit_and_predict) {          # returns a cross-validated probability for every batch
  p <- numeric(nrow(train))
  for (j in 1:10) p[fold == j] <- fit_and_predict(train[fold != j, ], train[fold == j, ])
  p
}
```

```{r}
#| label: compare
#| eval: false
cv_main <- cv_predict(function(tr, te) {
  fit <- glm(fail ~ reactor + shift + ..., family = binomial, data = tr)
  predict(fit, te, type = "response")
})
# ... and the other methods
results <- tibble(
  method = c("logistic, main effects", "..."),
  auc = c(as.numeric(auc(train$fail, cv_main)), ...),
  log_loss = c(...)
)
knitr::kable(results, digits = 3)
```

## 4. The chosen model and its threshold

<!-- Refit the chosen model to all 1,000 batches. Check its calibration (predicted against observed
     failure rates in groups), and justify the threshold from the costs. -->

```{r}
#| label: final-model
#| eval: false
final <- glm(fail ~ ..., family = binomial, data = train)
threshold <- cost_rescue / cost_rework
```

## 5. The test on new batches

<!-- Only now: read the results, predict the 250 new batches, and report the AUC, the confusion
     matrix at your threshold, and the cost against switching none and switching all. -->

```{r}
#| label: test
#| eval: false
results_new <- read_csv("data-raw/crystallization/new_batch_results.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
test <- new_batches |> left_join(results_new, by = "batch") |> clean()
p_test <- predict(final, test, type = "response")
flag <- p_test >= threshold
table(switched = flag, failed = test$fail)
c(model = cost_rescue * sum(flag) + cost_rework * sum(!flag & test$fail == 1),
  switch_none = cost_rework * sum(test$fail),
  switch_all = cost_rescue * nrow(test))
```

## 7. Does it work on R3?

<!-- Calibration, AUC and sensitivity at your threshold, by reactor, on the new batches. -->

```{r}
#| label: fairness
#| eval: false
test |>
  mutate(p = p_test) |>
  group_by(reactor) |>
  summarise(batches = n(), predicted = mean(p), observed = mean(fail),
            sensitivity = mean(p[fail == 1] >= threshold))
```
